name: CanonicalWireframe NodeTypes
purpose: Define CanonicalWireframe NodeTypes, Entity-local Property expectations, Required Links, abstraction interfaces and Binding semantics using the Canonical Contract Format resolved through the pinned immutable specification closure.

model.ccf: Defines canonical Entity and Property structure.
model.nodetypes: Define what Property types an Entity owns or is expected to own and which canonical Link attachments are mandatory for readiness.
model.rulesets: Interpret canonical Property values, Link semantics, endpoint roles, causality, flow, Link ownership/placement and unresolved impact direction.
model.projection: Consumes resolved semantic/readiness state but never becomes canonical authority.

rules: Entity.entity_type_ref resolves a NodeType by id inside the NodeTypes registry pinned by the containing artifact's immutable specification_ref.
NodeTypes describe Entity-local Property expectations and Required Link declarations.
NodeTypes do not define Property value semantics.
NodeTypes do not define Link direction, Link Property placement, flow semantics, causality, rendering, animation, geometry or layout.
Additional Properties may exist when their Rulesets resolve them.
Required Links declare canonical Link attachments that must exist for readiness.
Every effective Required Link entry is mandatory; Required Links are evaluated as AND, never OR.
Multiple Required Link entries may use the same link_type_ref and MUST NOT be deduplicated by Link type.
A concrete Required Link requirement is identified by requiring Entity id plus Required Link id.
Only canonical Link Properties explicitly bound to that concrete requirement through value.required_link_ref satisfy it.
A canonical Link may satisfy at most one concrete Required Link requirement.
Derived/projected Links and unbound ordinary Links do not satisfy Required Links.
Missing required Properties or Required Links make the Entity UNRESOLVED/unready; they do not make otherwise well-formed canonical data INVALID.
UNRESOLVED != INVALID
Abstraction inputs created by unresolved requirements are direct projections of concrete Required Link requirement instances.
No canonical Input Entity or intermediate boundary Link is created merely to expose a Required Link.
A projected Abstraction input preserves the original requirement identity: requiring Entity id + Required Link id.
Required Link evaluation is scoped to an explicit applicable specification version/set.
A changed Required Link definition produces a new specification version and MUST NOT rewrite an earlier specification version.
Historical readiness is evaluated against the specification version applicable to the historical state.
Current readiness is evaluated only against the currently applicable specification version.
Existing required_link_ref values MUST NOT be silently rebound, migrated, substituted or interpreted as satisfying a different Required Link id.
A historical required_link_ref whose requirement is not effective in the current specification contributes zero to current readiness but does not by itself invalidate the underlying semantic Link.
Specification version is evaluation context and MUST NOT be copied into required_link_ref.
Required Link ids are semantically immutable within one specification lineage.
A Required Link id removed from a later specification version remains reserved and MUST NOT be reused for a different requirement.
A semantic Required Link change creates a new Required Link id in a new specification version.
A canonical state/snapshot used for reconstructable readiness MUST carry a root-level specification_ref to one immutable specification-set artifact.
specification_ref is snapshot/evaluation provenance and MUST NOT be stored inside required_link_ref.
Historical readiness MUST NOT be claimed as reconstructed when the historical state lacks a resolvable immutable specification_ref.
Missing historical specification provenance MUST NOT be repaired by substituting the current specification.
A specification_ref used as readiness provenance MUST have immutable resolution.
For a preserved canonical state/snapshot, the same specification_ref value MUST always resolve to the same specification-set content.
Mutable aliases, moving tags, current/latest pointers, mutable branches and equivalent moving references MUST NOT be used as specification provenance.
CW does not require a specific specification_ref syntax, but the chosen reference mechanism MUST guarantee immutable resolution.
The applicable NodeTypes registry MUST validate as part of the specification set before model readiness evaluation begins.
An invalid NodeTypes/Rulesets specification set is INVALID_SPECIFICATION, not an INVALID_MODEL.
No READY/UNREADY model result may be produced from an INVALID_SPECIFICATION.
Free-text prose never satisfies NodeType Properties, Required Links, cardinalities, or readiness requirements.
READY means contract-conformant under the applicable specification; it does not assert real-world correctness or human intent.
Validation rules are version-scoped to the artifact being validated.
A historical NodeTypes artifact MUST be validated using the validation contract applicable to its own declared version.
Later validation requirements MUST NOT be applied retroactively to an earlier artifact.
A field introduced as mandatory in a later schema does not make an earlier artifact invalid when that field was not required by the earlier schema.
Applying newer validation semantics to an older artifact requires an explicit migration that creates a new artifact.
If the historical validation contract cannot be resolved, the validator MUST NOT silently substitute the latest contract.
Interpretation provenance immutability is transitive across the full evaluation dependency closure.
A mutable validation-contract dispatch target is forbidden for historical or current deterministic validation.
Short local ids such as ruleset_ref/entity_type_ref remain local to the pinned immutable closure and are not global mutable aliases.
NodeType/type/inheritance resolution is specification-scoped and MUST NOT fall back to a mutable current registry.
Historical NodeType interpretation uses the historical artifact's pinned specification closure.
Canonical READY does not prove that external implementation code conforms to the modeled NodeType semantics.
NodeTypes artifact version, CCF format version and specification_ref MUST be mutually compatible.
A deterministic but contradictory version combination is INVALID_SPECIFICATION; no version authority silently overrides another.

semantics.required_property_types: Minimum local Property types expected for readiness.
semantics.owned_property_types: Property types structurally associated with this NodeType. This is not a closed allow-list.
semantics.extends: Optional inheritance from other NodeTypes. Effective Required Links retain stable requirement ids through inheritance.
semantics.property_cardinality: Optional readiness constraints for local Property counts.
semantics.required_links: Independent mandatory canonical Link attachment requirements. Entries are conjunctive and retain stable ids.

semantics.id: Stable semantic requirement identity. Within one specification lineage, a Required Link id MUST NOT be reused for a different requirement meaning.
semantics.self_role: Semantic role the requiring Entity must occupy under the governing Link Ruleset.
semantics.min: Minimum number of distinct canonical Link Properties explicitly bound to this requirement instance.
semantics.max: Optional maximum number of canonical Link Properties explicitly bound to this requirement instance.
semantics.other_endpoint: Optional constraints on the opposite canonical endpoint.

required_link_schema.conjunction: Every effective Required Link entry is mandatory.
required_link_schema.duplicate_types: Two entries with the same link_type_ref remain separate requirements.

lineage_identity.replacement_rule: A semantically changed requirement receives a new Required Link id in a new specification version; the previous id is never recycled.

nodetypes.name: Generic
nodetypes.description: Minimal generic canonical node. Link ownership is available to all derived NodeTypes.

nodetypes.name: Input
nodetypes.description: Generic explicitly modeled inbound semantic node. It is not the canonical mechanism for Abstraction inputs created by Required Links.
constraints: Input is an ordinary explicit canonical Entity when a model needs an inbound semantic object.
Input does not encode or copy transported semantic type/signature.
Abstraction inputs caused by unsatisfied requirements are projected directly from concrete Required Link requirement instances.
An Input Entity is not created merely to expose a Required Link through an Abstraction boundary.
Input has no automatic Abstraction-interface authority merely because its NodeType id is input.

nodetypes.name: Output
nodetypes.description: The one generic canonical outbound Abstraction boundary NodeType.
constraints: Output is a real canonical Entity inside an Abstraction.
Output does not encode or copy transported semantic type/signature.
Transported semantics are derived from the explicit canonical internal attachment/binding or selected abstraction-local Binding identity.
Output creates no analogous inbound requirement.
Event boundaries use this same generic Output NodeType; no Event-specific Output NodeType exists.
An Output may consume an abstraction-local Binding only through the explicit canonical Binding-consumption relation defined by CW_RULESETS.
The consumed Binding is referenced by canonical Binding Entity identity, never by free-text Binding name.
An Output consuming a Binding derives transported semantic type/signature from that Binding's resolved source semantics.
The consumed Binding must belong to the same Abstraction semantic source as the Output.
Output semantics are independent from Required Link input projection; Abstraction inputs and outputs are not required to use symmetric canonical mechanisms.
Output is valid only inside exactly one Abstraction semantic source.
Top-level Workspace Output boundary use is forbidden.
An Output has exactly one resolved internal source relation at a time.
Its source is either one boundary_output relation from an internal canonical endpoint or one binding_consume relation from an Abstraction-local Binding.
Zero resolved source relations leaves Output UNRESOLVED; more than one active source relation is INVALID_MODEL.
The Output source and Output Entity belong to the same Abstraction semantic source.
Abstraction membership is resolved from canonical Abstraction source membership, never geometry.

nodetypes.name: Binding
constraints: Binding is valid only inside exactly one Abstraction semantic source.
Top-level Workspace Binding use is forbidden.
Cross-Abstraction Binding lookup is forbidden.
Binding Entity.name is the machine-significant Binding symbol and must be unique among Binding Entities in the same Abstraction.
A resolved Binding has exactly one incoming canonical semantic source at a time; absence while authoring is UNRESOLVED.
Binding accepts only canonical Link types whose governing Ruleset permits the Binding Entity in the relevant endpoint role.
Binding defines no universal special Link type and bypasses no Ruleset.
Binding semantic type/signature is derived from its connected canonical source endpoint and governing Ruleset and is never independently copied.
Output consumers select a Binding by canonical Binding Entity identity, not by free-text name.
Any number of Output nodes inside the same Abstraction may select the same Binding.
Binding lookup is non-spatial within its containing Abstraction.
Binding identity does not become part of the parent-level Abstraction interface.
Binding trace visualization is transient projection only and creates no canonical Link.
Output consumers reference a Binding by canonical Binding Entity identity through the explicit canonical Binding-consumption relation defined by CW_RULESETS.
Free-text Binding references are forbidden.
Any number of Output nodes inside the same Abstraction may consume the same Binding.
Binding trace visualization is transient projection only and MUST NOT be used as traversal authority.
Forward/backward semantic traversal across a Binding follows canonical Binding-consumption references defined by CW_RULESETS.
Every canonical source endpoint feeding a Binding belongs to the same Abstraction semantic source as the Binding.
A Binding source MUST NOT resolve from a parent-level Entity, another Abstraction, or an external mutable lookup.
Binding source scope is validated independently of Binding consumer scope.
Exactly one canonical inbound Link may provide the resolved Binding source; zero is UNRESOLVED and more than one is INVALID_MODEL.

nodetypes.name: File
nodetypes.description: Declares one external file that must be supplied to the implementation. The required filename is carried by the file Property.

nodetypes.name: File Output
nodetypes.description: Declares one externally materialized output file. The output filename is carried by the file Property.

nodetypes.name: API
nodetypes.description: API boundary or service node. API type plus canonical input/output refs are carried by its api Property.

nodetypes.name: Stream Input
nodetypes.description: External or upstream continuous data input.

nodetypes.name: User Input
nodetypes.description: Human-originated input surface. Concrete semantics are carried by Properties and Links.

nodetypes.name: User Output
nodetypes.description: Human-facing output surface. Concrete semantics are carried by Properties and Links.

nodetypes.name: Stream Source
nodetypes.description: Compatibility NodeType retained for existing CW models; semantically a stream_input specialization.

required_link_readiness.ready: Every effective Required Link requirement instance satisfies its own minimum through distinct canonical Link Properties explicitly bound using value.required_link_ref.
required_link_readiness.unready: At least one concrete Required Link requirement instance is below its minimum.
required_link_readiness.requirement_identity: requiring Entity id + Required Link id
required_link_readiness.same_link_type: Multiple requirements of the same Link type remain independent.
required_link_readiness.external_link_satisfaction: A valid external canonical Link carrying the concrete required_link_ref satisfies the original internal requirement.
required_link_readiness.historical: Evaluate against the historical specification context; preserve valid historical satisfaction.
required_link_readiness.current: Evaluate only current effective requirements; historical bindings to non-effective requirements contribute zero.
required_link_readiness.superseded_binding: Preserved canonical binding; does not satisfy a new/superseding requirement and does not by itself invalidate the semantic Link.

reference_resolution_cases.effective_and_matching: eligible to satisfy the current requirement
reference_resolution_cases.not_effective_in_applicable_spec: preserved canonical binding; readiness contribution 0; semantic Link is not invalid merely for this reason

readiness.ready: The Entity satisfies required Properties, Property cardinalities and every concrete Required Link requirement used by active evaluation.
readiness.unready: One or more expected NodeType Properties, Property cardinalities or Required Link attachments are unresolved or missing.

resolution.rule: Entity.entity_type_ref resolves a local NodeType id inside the explicitly active CW_NODETYPES registry. Local ids do not become globally unique merely by spelling.

binding_model.transported_semantics: derived from Binding resolved canonical source semantics
binding_model.semantic_traversal: follows canonical Binding-consumption relation, never trace-line geometry
binding_model.source_relation_selection: A Binding source is an active canonical Link for which the Binding occupies child_ref and whose governing Link Ruleset permits a Binding Entity at child_ref.
binding_model.source_search_scope: Search all canonical Links in the containing Abstraction semantic source, not only Properties physically stored on the Binding.
binding_model.source_endpoint_owner_resolution: If the source endpoint is an Entity, that Entity is the source owner; if it is a Property, use the Property's canonical owning Entity.

abstraction_input_model.external_projection: derived input socket/item on the Abstraction Entity
abstraction_input_model.transported_semantics: derived from the Required Link declaration, its governing Link Ruleset, semantic role and endpoint constraints
abstraction_input_model.satisfaction: An external canonical Link connected through the projected Abstraction input satisfies the original internal requirement by carrying the same value.required_link_ref.
abstraction_input_model.identity_rule: The external input representation does not receive an independent canonical identity; it represents the internal concrete Required Link requirement instance.

specification_versioning.principle: NodeType and Required Link evolution changes the applicable specification context; it does not rewrite historical canonical claims.
specification_versioning.mutation_rule: Changing an effective Required Link definition produces a new specification version rather than retroactively changing an earlier specification version.
specification_versioning.historical_evaluation: Historical readiness MUST resolve against the NodeType specification version applicable to that historical canonical state.
specification_versioning.current_evaluation: Current readiness MUST resolve against the currently applicable NodeType specification version.
specification_versioning.no_newer_substitution: A newer NodeType specification version MUST NOT be substituted when reconstructing historical readiness.
specification_versioning.requirement_identity: Concrete Required Link identity remains requiring Entity id + Required Link id; specification version is evaluation context and is not added to required_link_ref.
specification_versioning.lineage_rule: Required Link ids are semantically immutable across all versions of the same specification lineage.
specification_versioning.semantic_change_rule: If a Required Link changes meaning, constraints, semantic role, link type, or other identity-defining semantics, define a new Required Link id in the new specification version.
specification_versioning.removed_id_rule: A removed Required Link id remains reserved in the specification lineage and MUST NOT later be assigned a different meaning.
specification_versioning.provenance_requirement: Every canonical state/snapshot whose readiness must be reconstructable MUST carry an explicit specification_ref that resolves exactly one immutable specification-set artifact.
specification_versioning.specification_ref_semantics: specification_ref identifies the specification set under which that canonical state is evaluated. It is evaluation provenance, not part of required_link_ref.
specification_versioning.specification_ref_immutability: For a preserved historical snapshot, specification_ref MUST NOT be silently changed. A state evaluated under a different specification set is a different evaluation context and must be represented by an explicitly updated/new state or snapshot.
specification_versioning.specification_set_requirement: The referenced specification-set artifact MUST pin the full transitive evaluation dependency closure. NodeTypes, Rulesets, inheritance, CCF/format contracts, validation contracts and any other interpretation dependencies are either embedded immutable content or immutable-resolution references.
specification_versioning.missing_specification_ref: If historical readiness reconstruction is requested and the historical canonical snapshot does not identify its applicable immutable specification set, historical readiness is UNRESOLVED/UNPROVABLE; the runtime MUST NOT guess or substitute the current specification.

specification_ref_resolution.rule: For the lifetime of a preserved canonical state/snapshot, the same specification_ref value MUST always resolve to the same specification-set content.
allowed_identity_models: immutable artifact identity plus immutable version/revision
forbidden_reference_classes: any pointer whose target or content may change while the reference value stays the same
specification_ref_resolution.syntax_note: CW does not mandate one URI/hash syntax, but any chosen reference mechanism MUST guarantee immutable resolution.

specification_registry_validation.principle: The NodeTypes registry is part of the applicable specification set and MUST be internally valid before any canonical model readiness evaluation uses it.
checks: NodeType ids are unique within the registry
effective Required Link ids obey lineage immutability rules
Required Link min/max constraints are internally consistent
required_link self_role values can be resolved by the applicable Rulesets registry
every required_property_types and owned_property_types entry resolves an applicable Property Ruleset or the canonical Link specialization
every Required Link link_type_ref resolves exactly one Link Ruleset
every Required Link self_role resolves inside that Link Ruleset semantic_roles
every Binding source-scope constraint is machine-checkable
every Output source contract references declared Link Rulesets
specification_registry_validation.contract_selection: Validate this registry using the validation contract selected by this artifact's own declared version.

prose_boundary.principle: Free text may explain a model but is not machine-readable semantic authority.
prose_boundary.formalization_rule: Any constraint that must affect validation or readiness MUST be represented by an explicit structured canonical field, Property, Link, NodeType declaration, or Ruleset.

readiness_claim_boundary.ready_means: The Entity/model satisfies the machine-readable requirements of the applicable valid specification context.
ready_does_not_mean: the architecture matches the real world

validation_contract_versioning.principle: Validation rules are version-scoped. A NodeTypes artifact is validated against the validation contract applicable to that artifact's own declared format/schema version.
validation_contract_versioning.artifact_version_source: The artifact's own declared format/schema/version identity selects the applicable validation contract.
validation_contract_versioning.migration_required_for_new_rules: To subject an older artifact to newer validation requirements, perform an explicit migration that produces a new artifact governed by the newer contract.

missing_field_rule.not_required_in_artifact_version: Absence is not an error merely because a later validation contract requires the field.

validation_contract_versioning.validator_dispatch: A validator MUST resolve exactly one immutable validation-contract content from the artifact's version-scoped dispatch identity before validating the artifact.
validation_contract_versioning.unsupported_historical_contract: If the required historical validation contract cannot be resolved, the implementation MUST NOT substitute the latest contract or invent a semantic result.

local_semantic_ref.meaning: An identity resolved only inside an already pinned immutable canonical/specification artifact or registry closure. It is not an external locator.
local_semantic_ref.rule: Local semantic refs are safe only because the containing artifact/registry closure is immutable and uniquely selected. They MUST NOT silently escape to a mutable external lookup namespace.

interpretation_provenance_ref.meaning: A reference whose resolved content can change validation, interpretation, inheritance, readiness or historical reconstruction.
examples: external NodeTypes/Rulesets registry dependency when not embedded
interpretation_provenance_ref.rule: The same reference value MUST always resolve to the same content.

runtime_or_domain_ref.meaning: A domain/runtime reference whose mutability is governed by its own semantic contract and which is not automatically evaluation provenance.
runtime_or_domain_ref.immutable_external_resolution_required: only when another contract elevates it into interpretation provenance

evaluation_dependency_closure.principle: Immutable specification provenance applies to the full transitive interpretation/evaluation dependency closure, not only to the root specification_ref.
closure_members: NodeTypes registry content used by evaluation
Rulesets registry content used by evaluation
CCF/format/schema contract content used to interpret the artifacts
validation contract content used to validate the artifacts
any other external contract whose resolved content can change model validity or readiness
evaluation_dependency_closure.dependency_rule: Every closure member MUST either be embedded in an immutable parent artifact or be reached through an immutable-resolution interpretation_provenance_ref.
evaluation_dependency_closure.transitive_rule: If a closure member itself references another interpretation dependency, the same rule applies recursively.
forbidden: immutable root manifest containing a mutable NodeTypes pointer
immutable root manifest containing a mutable Rulesets pointer
immutable root manifest selecting a validation contract through a moving alias
any transitive interpretation dependency changing while the root provenance reference stays unchanged
evaluation_dependency_closure.not_applied_automatically_to: runtime/domain references that do not participate in interpretation, validation or readiness

validation_contract_resolution.principle: Version-scoped validation is deterministic only if validation-contract resolution itself is immutable.
validation_contract_resolution.dispatch_key: The artifact's declared validation/format identity and version as defined by its format lineage.
validation_contract_resolution.if_explicit_validation_contract_ref_is_u: It is an interpretation_provenance_ref and MUST have immutable resolution.
validation_contract_resolution.historical_rule: A historical artifact's dispatch key MUST always select the same historical validation-contract content.

ccf_ref_semantics.rule: ccf_ref is not permission to resolve a mutable 'current CCF'. Its applicable CCF/format contract must be part of the pinned immutable evaluation dependency closure.
ccf_ref_semantics.local_key_rule: A short value such as CANONICAL_CONTRACT_FORMAT MAY be used as a local semantic key only when the immutable specification set uniquely binds that key to immutable CCF/format-contract content.

registry_ref_semantics.rule: registry_ref identifies this registry inside the pinned immutable specification set; it is not an external mutable registry locator.

immutable_resolution_bootstrap.principle: Immutable-resolution requirements recurse through interpretation dependencies until reaching embedded immutable content or an immutable identity mechanism whose same-key/same-content property is guaranteed externally.
acceptable_roots: immutable artifact revision identity enforced by storage
immutable version-to-contract mapping enforced by the format/validator host
immutable_resolution_bootstrap.host_obligation: The host may provide the final immutable identity mechanism, but it MUST satisfy same identity -> same content and MUST NOT expose mutable aliases as provenance.

semantic_reference_resolution.entity_type_ref: Entity.entity_type_ref resolves only against the NodeTypes registry pinned in that artifact's immutable specification closure.
semantic_reference_resolution.extends: NodeType inheritance ids resolve only inside the same pinned NodeTypes/specification closure.
semantic_reference_resolution.required_link_ruleset_refs: Required Link link_type_ref/self_role interpretation uses the Rulesets registry in the same pinned specification closure.
semantic_reference_resolution.historical: Historical Entity NodeTypes and inheritance are interpreted using the historical artifact's specification_ref.

model_implementation_correspondence.READY_scope: NodeType and Required Link readiness concerns only modeled machine-readable semantics.
model_implementation_correspondence.formalization: Any such constraint that must affect readiness must be represented by structured canonical semantics governed by Rulesets.

version_identity_coherence.rule: CW NodeTypes artifacts MUST be interpreted only when their artifact version, CCF format version and pinned specification_ref resolve to one compatible immutable interpretation context.

output_source_contract.direct_source: boundary_output parent_ref is the internal canonical semantic endpoint and child_ref is the Output Entity.
output_source_contract.binding_source: binding_consume parent_ref is the Binding Entity and child_ref is the Output Entity.
output_source_contract.transported_semantics: derived from the one resolved source; never copied as a second authority
output_source_contract.membership: source and Output must resolve inside the same Abstraction semantic source
